PullRequest.Title: chat: clamp sticky requests that start with a Markdown block
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

A request pinned by chat sticky scroll is clamped to two lines, but only when it starts with a paragraph. A request that starts with a list, heading, quote, code block or table was pinned at its full height, which takes up much of the transcript.

This applies the same clamp to whichever block comes first. It is a CSS-only change in `chat.css`, plus a test.

- **Lists, headings and quotes** are clamped to two lines like a paragraph, with "…" appended when the request continues after the block.
- **A leading code block or table** has no lines of text to clamp, so it is cut off at the height of two lines.
- **A code block or table inside a list item or quote** is hidden. The line clamp skips it and would otherwise show it in full.
- **A list keeps the margins of its items**, so its pinned bubble is 8px taller than one with plain text.

One behavior change to be aware of: a request that starts with a horizontal rule, such as pasted front matter, now pins as only the rule, where before it was pinned in full. I left that as is.

There is no tracking issue for this.

## How to test

1. Set `chat.stickyScroll.enabled` and `chat.experimental.stickyScroll.enabled` to `true`.
2. Send a request that starts with a Markdown list of long items, and get a response long enough to scroll.
3. Scroll the request out of view. The pinned request shows two lines of the list, like a plain-text request does.
4. Repeat with requests that start with a heading, a quote, a fenced code block and a table.

## Validation

Everything below ran locally with this diff applied on an older `main` commit (699a5b3c877) rather than on this branch's base, because the dependencies of the current base did not install in my environment. Between the two, the changed files differ only in unrelated places.

- Sticky tests of the changed test file: 59 passing.
  ```
  ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListWidget.test.ts --grep "[Ss]ticky|pinned request"
  ```
- The whole changed test file: 195 passing, 1 failing. The failure is `falls back to a full refresh when the request or the transcript changes`, which fails the same way without this change and passes intermittently when run alone.
  ```
  ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListWidget.test.ts
  ```
- Sticky tests of related files: 46 passing.
  ```
  ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListRenderer.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/promptTimeline/promptTimelineVisibility.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatView.test.ts --grep "[Ss]ticky"
  ```
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run stylelint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chat.css`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatListWidget.test.ts`: passed.
- The new test fails with the stylesheet change reverted. It fails in `createTranscript`, because the request with a long list is then not pinned at all in the test's 300px-tall view.

Not run: any of this on the branch's own base, a launched build, the full unit suite, and the integration and smoke tests. I checked each block type visually only on a static page that loads `chat.css` with mock request markup in Chromium 150, not in a running VS Code.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll a request beginning with a list, heading, or quote into the chat sticky header.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing tree controller selects and renders the sticky request, applies CSS, probes its height, and updates the sticky source range before painting. The diff changes the first block's presentation, not the scheduling or geometry-read locations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser style resolution, layout, offsetHeight, and getBoundingClientRect measurements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one sticky row per widget; range passes measure currently rendered request templates plus the one sticky template, not every historical request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same renderer and measurements ran before the PR. Paragraph-first requests were already clamped; nonparagraph-first blocks retained their full layout height. The diff generalizes the clamp and hides subsequent siblings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial layout and height measurements precede the visible sticky-header paint.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One pinned request, whose first block may contain many list items, nested quotes, or long text; ordinary transcript rows remain virtualized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Main-thread rendering; ChatListWidget limits sticky scroll to one item. Source-range measurement requests share a per-frame pass. Equal sticky state is retained, and push-out-only changes update position rather than reconstructing content.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold sticky rendering uses the existing Markdown renderer. Warm state retains the sticky DOM; request content is keyed by request ID and dataId/editing text, with cached widths and source ranges. None of these cache or invalidation rules changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the one-row bound, unchanged rendering path, retained-state checks, and unchanged measurement batching from inspected callers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser-specific costs of line-clamping complex blocks are not measured. Additional selector matching alone does not establish a concrete regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: CSS changes presentation without adding repeated rendering, geometry reads, boundary fan-out, or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pin a request beginning with a fenced code block or table, including code blocks or tables nested in a leading list or quote.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing Markdown parsing constructs the request content, code editors and table scroll wrappers where applicable; browser layout then measures the sticky bubble. The new CSS caps leading nontext block height and removes nested code/table boxes from layout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct or reuse code-editor widgets and in-memory text models, and lay out code editors and scrollable tables.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-code-block rendering within the one sticky request; model creation occurs on editor-pool misses, not per table cell. No filesystem, database, subprocess, or IPC call is added by these CSS rules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same content parts and editors were constructed before the PR. Leading code/table blocks and nested code/table boxes were laid out visibly; the changed rules cap or hide them without adding renderer invocations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Editor construction/rendering occurs on the existing initial sticky-render path; layout determines bubble geometry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Measure the rendered sticky row after applying the new CSS height and display constraints.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One row per initial or changed sticky-state render.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same dynamic-height probe measured the previously taller content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed before final sticky-row height is committed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Code blocks, code text, and table cells within a single request; all Markdown construction was already performed before CSS presentation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous Markdown/code-editor construction on the main thread for one pinned request. The existing EditorPool uses request/block keys and retains at most two idle editors. No new asynchronous queue or concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The editor pool and sticky-state reuse remain unchanged. Cold editor creation constructs an in-memory vscodeChatCodeBlock text model; warm rendering can use the existing keyed pool. CSS hiding does not create a new allocation owner or prevent existing disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that content construction and pool lifecycle are unchanged, based on the Markdown constructor, renderCodeBlock, CodeBlockPart model ownership, and sticky-template disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact layout savings or browser quirks are unmeasured; no concrete increase in work or retention is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance bug. Hiding already-constructed editors is not a newly introduced eager-allocation mechanism; recommending lazy construction here would expand scope into pre-existing behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continue scrolling, stream a response, or resize the transcript while a Markdown request is pinned.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing scroll/state updates and resize-driven source-range measurement maintain header position and geometry. Streaming response updates can refresh sticky state but do not require a new network operation to clamp the request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser geometry measurements and sticky-header position/style updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Measurements are grouped per pending frame across rendered templates; one pinned request is updated. Position-only scroll transitions avoid full reconstruction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical scheduling, geometry-read count, sticky-state equality checks, and source-height suppression existed before the PR. Only the CSS-computed geometry of nonparagraph-first sticky requests changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Layout must settle for an accurate visible header after resize; ordinary retained scrolling does not reconstruct the request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Scroll and resize event frequency, visible request templates, and one sticky row. Transcript history does not multiply the changed CSS into one pinned row per request.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Main-thread UI work with a shared per-frame source-range pass and next-frame sticky-state refresh. StickyScrollWidget skips equal state and updates only the last row's top for position-only transitions. Sticky rows are excluded from source item-height notifications.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cached source widths/ranges and retained sticky state remain intact. CSS does not change cache keys, negative-cache handling, refresh coalescing, or content identity.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in unchanged scheduling and finite geometry updates from the inspected renderer and tree implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No profiling of sustained scrolling or resizing was performed. There is no traced diff-induced feedback loop or loss of coalescing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression: the diff neither introduces per-event reconstruction nor defeats existing batching, retention, or source-height safeguards.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the added Markdown-block sticky-height unit test.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test sequentially creates transcripts, waits for layout to stabilize, pins requests, and reads browser geometry/computed pseudo-element content.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct test DOM/widgets, await animation frames, and read getBoundingClientRect/getComputedStyle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Nine fixed fixtures; geometry assertions and stabilization waits are bounded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This specific fixed-size coverage did not exist; surrounding tests already use the same transcript helper and stabilization mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations contribute only to this unit test's duration, not application startup or interaction latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed set of nine transcript fixtures; eight code lines and a small fixed table. No user-controlled unbounded test loop is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Nine bounded helper invocations run sequentially; model/services are mocked. Existing waitForStableLayout is capped at 120 frames per call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each fixture creates its own widget and renderer pools; fixture disposables belong to the existing suite-owned DisposableStore and are released by teardown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the fixed fixture count, bounded waits, mocked services, and suite-owned cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Test duration can depend on headless animation-frame throttling, but no measured timeout or unbounded retained resource is demonstrated.
Scenarios.Verdict: Normal bounded test coverage, not an actionable product performance regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across the complete two-file inventory and all three diff hunks against base 671d82d2d8146041c57b5b51787dd57d2daf3ab7. Traced sticky rendering, measurement/coalescing, cache ownership, code-editor construction, and test-fixture cleanup. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions found. No concrete historical performance regression fix established for blame-based learning. Static read-only analysis; browser timing and profiling were unavailable. The supporting guide tool returned only a truncated preview; learned-regression guidance was fully available.
